en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Saeed Bin Janaah, from Hammad, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz who said,

‘We lodged at Al-Medina, so we went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘Where are you lodged at?’ So we said, ‘At so and so, the owner of the singing slave-girls’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Be honourable’. So, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, we did not know what he<sup>asws</sup> intended by it, and we thought that he<sup>asws</sup> was saying that we should be graceful to him. So we returned to him<sup>asws</sup>, so we said, ‘We do not know what you<sup>asws</sup> intended by your<sup>asws</sup> words: ‘Be honourable’’.
So heasws said: ‘Have you all not hear the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic in Hisazwj Book [25:72] and when they pass by what is vain, they pass by nobly’.
en.sarwar: 9. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Sa‘id ibn Junah from Hammad from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz who has said the following: “Once we arrived in al-Madinah and visited abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who asked us, ‘Where have you lodged?’ We said, ‘It is with so and so, the owner of singing slave-girls.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must remain honorable.’ By Allah we did not understand what he (the Imam) meant and we thought perhaps he wants us to be kind to him (owner of the lodging). We returned to him (the Imam) and asked, ‘We did not understand your words, ‘Be honorable.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Have you not heard the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘When they pass by useless things they pass honorably.’
